entries.clue: No trace of husband or nephew in Hibernia or lands further south (6)

indicatorNotes.No trace of: leaving no trace of a letter means taking it out

blocks.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland
h = husband, removed
n = nephew, removed

annotation.surface: A geography lesson tracing a family's absence from Ireland and the countries to its south.
annotation.walkthrough: Strip H and N from HIBERNIA and IBERIA is left; the two names are a letter pair apart, and the peninsula does lie south of Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, lands well south of Ireland.

entries.clue: Solve this clue to beget grand urban construction! (11,4)

annotation.definition: Solve this clue to beget grand urban construction!

indicatorNotes.Solve: solving a puzzle means working its letters out into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: An invitation to crack the clue and conjure up a great city monument.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: rearranging BEGET GRAND URBAN produces the answer, and the answer is itself a grand piece of urban construction, Berlin's neoclassical gateway.
annotation.definitionFit: The Brandenburg Gate is a monumental eighteenth-century gateway in Berlin, a grand urban construction.

entries.clue: Second life for polystyrene wall filling (7)

indicatorNotes.filling: the answer is the filling inside the words polystyrene wall

blocks.note: polystyRENE WALl

annotation.surface: A tip for recycling polystyrene as cavity-wall insulation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Filling' looks like insulation stuffed into a wall; it is really the instruction to look inside the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A renewal gives something a fresh start, a second life.

entries.clue: Verify eccentric Cartesian (9)

indicatorNotes.eccentric: eccentric means off-centre, out of normal order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Checking the claims of an odd follower of Descartes.
annotation.walkthrough: Cartesian means relating to Descartes, the philosopher of doubt, which suits a clue about verifying things.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to establish for certain that something is true.

entries.clue: Six slices of tripe set alongside old Spanish bread (6)

indicatorNotes.Six slices of: six letters are sliced out of the phrase that follows

blocks.note: triPE SET Alongside

annotation.surface: A menu of tripe served with old Spanish bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not the loaf the menu suggests; the peseta was Spain's currency before the euro.
annotation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's unit of money until 2002, and bread is slang for money.

entries.clue: Fruit and asparagus tip falling to the floor (5)

indicatorNotes.falling to the floor: in a down entry, the top letter drops to the bottom

blocks.note: a spear is an asparagus shoot
in a down entry the top letter drops to the bottom

annotation.surface: Fruit and asparagus dropped on the kitchen floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' makes you want the first letter A, but here it means the whole shoot, a spear; its first letter then sinks to the foot of this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: the pear is an orchard fruit, the clue's 'Fruit' covering it as a category.

entries.clue: See opera – ENO – never seeing energy in its star? (7)

indicatorNotes.never seeing: never seeing a letter means it is nowhere to be found in the result

blocks.note: the letters as printed
e = energy; every E in the string is removed

annotation.surface: Advice to see an English National Opera production that never shows any energy in its lead.
annotation.walkthrough: ENO is English National Opera. Delete all four Es from SEE OPERA ENO and the remaining letters spell SOPRANO in order, no rearranging needed.
annotation.definitionFit: The soprano is usually the star of an opera, the 'its' pointing back to the opera.

entries.clue: Sherlock’s defining characteristic heard in final moments (3,4,8)

indicatorNotes.heard: heard tells you to go by the sound

blocks.note: Sherlock Holmes's trait

annotation.surface: What makes Sherlock Holmes who he is, overheard at the climax of a story.
annotation.walkthrough: Say 'the Holmes trait' quickly and it runs into THE HOME STRAIGHT, the last stretch of a racecourse before the finish.
annotation.definitionFit: The home straight is the final stretch of a race, hence the last stage or final moments of anything.

entries.clue: Spooner tells us one seasoning food’s approaching being delightful (2,4,2,3)

indicatorNotes.Spooner tells us: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a spice seasons food; nigh = approaching

annotation.surface: Spooner announcing that a spice for the food is on its way, which sounds lovely.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the SP of 'spice' with the N of 'nigh' and 'a spice's nigh' becomes 'as nice as pie'.
annotation.definitionFit: As nice as pie is an idiom for very pleasant, delightful.

entries.clue: School leavers’ event in which patriotic songs belted out at last? (4)

annotation.definition2: in which patriotic songs belted out at last?

blocks.note: a school-leavers' dance

blocks.clueFragment: in which patriotic songs belted out at last?
blocks.note: the BBC's summer concert season, whose Last Night ends in massed patriotic singing

annotation.surface: A leavers' party that ends with everyone singing patriotic songs.
annotation.walkthrough: The BBC Proms are a London summer concert season whose Last Night famously ends with patriotic songs such as Rule, Britannia! sung by the whole hall; 'at last' plays on that Last Night.
annotation.definitionFit: A prom is both a school-leavers' dance and one of the Proms concerts.

entries.clue: Occupying this inventor? Safety, principally! (4)

indicatorNotes.principally: principally = in first place, taking the first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Occupying This Inventor Safety

annotation.surface: A question about what preoccupied an inventor, answered: safety above all.
annotation.walkthrough: Elisha Otis invented the safety brake that made passenger lifts trustworthy, so the whole clue both spells and describes him.
annotation.definitionFit: Elisha Otis's great invention was the safety elevator, so safety did occupy him.

entries.clue: Scarlet towers over not-so-bright stars (3,6)

blocks.note: scarlet = red
to dwarf is to tower over

annotation.surface: A scarlet figure looming over dim celebrities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stars' reads as celebrities, and 'not-so-bright' as dim-witted; both are astronomical here.
annotation.definitionFit: Red dwarfs are small, cool stars far fainter than the Sun.

entries.clue: Overly loud American, looking back, going on (5)

indicatorNotes.looking back: looking back turns the letters to face the other way

blocks.note: overly = too
f = forte, loud in music
a = American

annotation.surface: A brash American reminiscing and rambling on.
annotation.walkthrough: TOO, F and A are read backwards together, giving AFOOT.
annotation.definitionFit: Something afoot is under way, going on.

entries.clue: Philippine city’s enthralling student paper (7)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: enthralling = holding captive, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: Manila is the Philippine capital
l = learner, the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A Philippine city captivating a student newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a student newspaper, but it is the tough brown paper once made from Manila hemp, so the city lends its name twice over.
annotation.definitionFit: Manilla is strong brown paper used for envelopes and folders.

entries.clue: They split – to do the reverse! (7)

annotation.definition: They split – to do the reverse!

blocks.note: the surface pushes 'split up'; here it is slang for leave in a hurry
they run off in order to be joined, in marriage

annotation.surface: A couple breaking up in order to do the opposite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as separate, but it is slang for leave in a hurry; elopers run off precisely to unite, the reverse of splitting up.
annotation.definitionFit: Elopers run away secretly to marry.

entries.clue: Troubles, including yoga, tai chi etc (9)

blocks.note: to exercise someone is to worry them
yoga and tai chi are examples, hence the plural and 'etc'

annotation.surface: Worries that turn out to include taking up yoga and tai chi.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Troubles' is a verb here: an issue that exercises you is one that bothers you.
annotation.definitionFit: Exercises means both worries (verb) and physical activities such as yoga (noun).

entries.clue: Called out: Starter’s cooking – taste? (7)

blocks.note: the starter, soup, is on the stove

annotation.surface: A cook shouting that the first course is on, and offering a taste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soup's on!' is the cook's call that food is ready; said aloud it matches soupçon, a French borrowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny amount, a taste.

entries.clue: Does the groundwork for gits? (4)

blocks.note: to sod is to cover ground with turf
sod and git are both mild British insults

annotation.surface: Someone doing all the preparation for a bunch of idiots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groundwork' means preparation in the surface but is literal here: laying sods of turf on the ground. Git is British slang for an unpleasant person.
annotation.definitionFit: Sods is both a verb (lays turf) and a plural noun for annoying people.

entries.clue: He makes little effort, braggart downgraded at first (7)

indicatorNotes.downgraded at first: the first letter drops a grade, from B to C

blocks.note: a braggart boasts
grade B becomes grade C, replacing the first letter

annotation.surface: A slacker who used to be a braggart, taken down a peg.
annotation.walkthrough: Exam grades supply the swap: BOASTER falls from a B to a C, giving COASTER.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who coasts gets by with little effort.

entries.clue: Earl, scoundrel, overcome by booze, making misstep (7)

indicatorNotes.overcome by: overcome by = surrounded, swallowed up by

blocks.note: e = earl
rum is booze
a rat is a scoundrel, sitting inside RUM

annotation.surface: A drunken earl and a rogue making a false step.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overcome by booze' is the familiar drunk-aristocrat picture, but it is the container signal: the scoundrel sits inside the drink, and the earl's letter stands in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin for 'error', erratum names a mistake in print, a misstep in the figurative sense.

entries.clue: About to eat, having swallowed whiskey and claret (3,4)

indicatorNotes.having swallowed: one piece swallows another, holding it inside

blocks.note: re = about
dine = eat
W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet, swallowed by DINE

annotation.surface: Someone about to have dinner, having already downed a whiskey and a claret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whiskey' spelt with an E is the NATO alphabet's word for W, the usual signal for a single letter. 'About' opens the entry as a preposition, not an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, one particular red wine.

entries.clue: Everyman getting fourth of rounds, suppressing touch of angst, reluctant to pay (4)

indicatorNotes.fourth of: fourth of names a position in the word, so only the letter in fourth place is taken
indicatorNotes.touch of: a touch is just the first letter

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, is 'me'
rouNds
first letter of angst, held inside ME N

annotation.surface: The setter getting a round in, anxious and tight-fisted about it.
annotation.walkthrough: MEN holds A inside it: ME(A)N. A setter often names himself to mean ME.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of stingy: a mean person hates parting with money.

entries.clue: Morning deity rejected doctrine (5)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected comes from the Latin for thrown back, so the letters are thrown back to front

blocks.note: am = morning
a god is a deity

annotation.surface: A dawn god whose teaching has been cast aside.
annotation.walkthrough: AM and GOD run backwards together, making DOGMA.
annotation.definitionFit: A dogma is a doctrine laid down as beyond dispute.

entries.clue: Quack, then maraud wildly in a kind of story (9)

indicatorNotes.wildly: behaving wildly means out of control, so the letters are thrown out of their order

blocks.note: a quack is a doctor, informally a doc
anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: A duck's noise followed by a rampage, as in some wild tale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quack' looks like a duck's call but is a (fake) doctor. 'Then' simply orders the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A docudrama dramatises real events, a kind of story.

entries.clue: Reads about faces (5)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

annotation.surface: Someone reading up about faces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faces' is a verb here, as in faces danger, and 'about' is the anagram signal rather than a preposition.
annotation.definitionFit: To dare something is to face up to it.

entries.clue: Creating three of M*A*S*H’s characters? (11)

blocks.note: reads as inventing three people; really means adding three marks
not Hawkeye and co. but the typed stars in the title

annotation.surface: Inventing three of the cast of the TV series M*A*S*H.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests the cast, Hawkeye and friends; it means typed characters, and the title's three stars are asterisks.
annotation.definitionFit: Asterisking is marking with asterisks, the three star characters in M*A*S*H.

entries.clue: Bride’s delirious, in bits (6)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters, the apostrophe ignored

annotation.surface: An overjoyed bride, falling apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In bits' reads as emotionally in pieces; 'in' is only the join and 'bits' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: debris is the scattered fragments left when something breaks apart.

entries.clue: In southeast, Dutch to leave S African grassland thin (6)

indicatorNotes.In: the grassland goes in the compass point
indicatorNotes.to leave: to leave means to go away, so the letter for Dutch departs from the grassland

blocks.note: SE = southeast, split around the rest
the veldt is open South African grassland
D = Dutch, removed from VELDT

annotation.surface: Dutch settlers leaving the sparse grassland of south-east Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: The veldt is open South African grassland; the spelling without D is also accepted, which is what the deletion leaves. 'Thin' looks like it describes the grassland but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful, thin.
